text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: billing-usage-pipeline-lag for org-wide metering - sev2. Symptoms: consumer lag on kafka topic `usage.events.v1`, downstream aggregator queue growth, invoice-generator failing reconciliation checks. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/billing-metering
PagerDuty: Pager fired to oncall: Priya. Escalation policy: 10min -> eng-sre -> billing-ops.
Priya (oncall): ack, I'm on it. grabbing logs now. assigning Alex for infra help.
Alex (eng-sre): on call too, jumping in. any customer-facing impacts reported?
Maya (support): CS noticed 3 customers flagged invoices as "blocked - reconciliation error" earlier this morning. Tickets: #3245, #3248, #3251. They were held before charge.
Sam (billing-ops): confirming invoice-generator run failed reconciliation step due to missing consumption windows for 2026-03-14 02:00-03:00 UTC. Likely pipeline gap.
Priya (oncall): initial hypothesis: consumer group stalled, offsets not committed -> downstream aggregator missed ~200k events (~1.2M tokens). Affects final invoice delta calculation.
Alex (eng-sre): grabbing consumer metrics: `kafka.consumer_lag{group="metering-consumer"}` shows spike to 120k. consumer process host metering-01 shows OOM events around 02:03.
Priya (oncall): taking mitigation steps: 1) scale metering consumers x2 2) restart metering container on metering-01 3) kick off backfill/reprocess job in dry-run to estimate delta.
Priya (oncall): executing restart:
```bash
ssh metering-01
sudo systemctl restart metering-consumer
```
Alex (eng-sre): restarted container, logs show consumer rejoined group but processing is slow due to large backoff from retry policy. Temporarily bumped consumer parallelism to 6.
Priya (oncall): starting reprocess estimation job (dry-run):
```bash
python tools/reprocess.py --topic usage.events.v1 --from-offset 1234500 --to-offset 1350000 --dry-run --output /tmp/reprocess-estimate.json
```
Priya (oncall): dry-run estimate: ~1.15M missing tokens across 27 orgs. Most impacted: org-A, org-C (internal P0s).
Sam (billing-ops): thanks. We will pause invoice run for impacted cohort and mark invoices as "pending investigation" to avoid wrong charges. I'll file escalation to Finance.
Maya (support): I'll message the priority customers with a brief note: "We're investigating a billing delay and holding invoices; no charges will be posted until we confirm usage." Drafting now. @Sam want to review?
Sam (billing-ops): pls cc finance. I'll prepare an internal Slack thread for billing execs.
Priya (oncall): reprocess job started in full mode. Command:
```bash
python tools/reprocess.py --topic usage.events.v1 --from-offset 1234500 --to-offset 1350000 --output /var/backfills/1771001234.json
```
IncidentBot: backfill job created: backfill-id=bf-1771001234. Monitor: https://redwood.internal/backfills/bf-1771001234
Alex (eng-sre): ingestion catching up after scaling. consumer_lag down to 8k. Still watching headroom on aggregator. Consider temporary rate-limit for non-critical feature sampling to reduce ingestion pressure.
Priya (oncall): ran integrity checks on reprocessed data; numbers align with expected window. Reconciler dry-run shows delta positive for most orgs (i.e., missing usage will increase invoice amounts).
Sam (billing-ops): Finance prefers us to run a reconciliation diff and include audit bundle before unblocking invoice generation. ETA for full reprocess completion ~40m.
Maya (support): customer messages queued, sending now for top-3 impacted customers. Template: "We're holding your invoice while we validate usage. We'll update within 4 hours."
PagerDuty: Escalation: if not acked by next tier in 10m, will escalate to billing manager.
Priya (oncall): handoff note for next oncall (in 2h): backfill-id=bf-1771001234, reprocess ETA ~40m, current status: consumer_lag=stable ~5k, invoices paused for cohort. Steps to finish: monitor backfill stream, run reconciler, publish audit bundle, unpause invoice run after signoff from Sam.
Priya (oncall): tagging BillingRunbookBot for checklist verification.
BillingRunbookBot: Runbook check OK: required steps logged (restart, scale, backfill, reconciliation). Suggested post-incident actions: increase consumer memory limits, add OOM alerts, add passive rate-limit for sampling traffic.
Alex (eng-sre): created PR to bump metering-consumer memory and adjust retry policy. Link: https://redwood.internal/pull/infra/3456
Sam (billing-ops): reconciler completed. Audit bundle generated: s3://billing-audits/bf-1771001234/audit.zip. Reviewing diffs now.
Priya (oncall): reprocess finished. final consumer_lag=0. Reconciler diff: total delta +1,174,332 tokens across 27 orgs.
Sam (billing-ops): Finance reviewed audit bundle; approved unpause for invoice-generator for non-critical cohorts. We'll run a targeted invoice job for impacted cohort with additional verification.
Maya (support): updated customer messages: "We've validated usage and will run your invoice shortly; no unexpected charges will be applied retroactively without notice." Customers acknowledged.
Priya (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. Creating postmortem checklist: root cause: OOM on metering-01 consumer due to increased sampling traffic + tight memory config; detection: pager fired via consumer lag alerts; impact: invoice generation paused for a small cohort (~27 orgs), potential underreported usage recovered via backfill, customer-facing invoice delays.
Priya (oncall): next steps assigned: Alex -> bump container memory & tune retry; Sam -> runbook update for invoice-hold communication; Ops -> add OOM alert to PagerDuty policy; Maya -> finalize CS templates.
Sam (billing-ops): filing invoice follow-up tickets and updating Finance.
IncidentBot: incident marked mitigated by Priya. Incident timeline recorded under https://redwood.internal/incidents/1771001234
PagerDuty: Pager acknowledged by Priya, resolved after mitigation. :white_check_mark:
Priya (oncall): handing off to next oncall: @Devon will own any follow-ups. Leaving final note: monitor backfill metrics and customer tickets for 24h.
Devon: acked, will monitor.
Priya (oncall): thanks everyone. Good collaboration. :thumbsup:
